activities.title: 6. Reconstruct Telephone Dialogue
activities.instruction: Put the sentences in order (1-9) to form a coherent telephone conversation.

steps.text: What are we going to do tonight Peter?
Well, there is a music festival in New Smyrni square tonight.
I want to go. Would you like to come?
What will we see if we choose to go there?
We will see dances from various parts of Greece. I heard there are great bands and musicians, too.
What instruments are we going to hear?
All kinds. Most of the bands are led by the clarinet, but we will enjoy the bagpipe, and the lute, too. Well, what do you say?
It sounds nice. Where shall we meet?
At the corner of Aigaiou and Eleftheriou Venizelou Street, at seven.
Ok. But wait for me if I'm a little late.

activities.title: 1. Conditionals Type 1 (Real Conditions)
activities.instruction: Complete the sentences with the correct form of the verbs in brackets.

sentences.text: If you [blank:go] to the concert, you will listen to your favourite songs.
If I [blank:do not go] to the concert, I may go to the cinema.
If you decide to go to the concert, [blank:will you telephone] me?
You [blank:will not forget] their passionate singing if you choose to attend their performance.
If pupils [blank:study] classical music, they may become more intelligent.
You must [blank:practise] very hard if you want to be a great musician.
If I am late for the concert, please [blank:wait] for me.

activities.title: 4. Giving Advice with 'If I were you'
activities.instruction: Give helpful advice in each difficult situation using 'If I were you, I would...'.

scenarios.problem: Your friend Panos is bullied on the way home from school.
scenarios.advice: If I were you, I would tell your parents and your headteacher immediately. You shouldn't walk home alone.

scenarios.problem: Your sister wants to buy a guitar but lacks the money.
scenarios.advice: If I were you, I would save my weekly pocket money and do some household chores to earn extra cash.

scenarios.problem: Your sister talks on the phone instead of doing homework.
scenarios.advice: If I were you, I would switch off my mobile phone during study hours so you can concentrate and get good marks.

activities.title: 5. Mixed Conditionals (Type 1 & Type 2)
activities.instruction: Complete the sentences with the correct verb forms.

sentences.text: If I [blank:do not become] a musician, I will become an actor.
If I [blank:could] play the saxophone, I would join the city band.
If it [blank:does not rain] tomorrow, we will go to the festival.
I [blank:would buy] a beautiful house on the beach if I had a lot of money.
If you go to the funfair, please [blank:buy] a T-shirt for me.
You [blank:must study] harder if you want to become a band conductor.
sentences.answer: must study / should study / will have to study

sentences.text: If I [blank:met] Madonna, I would ask for an autograph.
You dance so well! If I [blank:were] you, I would start ballet lessons!
If I [blank:saw] a wild animal in the city centre, I would be surprised and I would call the police!

activities.title: 6. Conversational Reactions
activities.instruction: Choose the most appropriate conversational response (a, b, or c).

items.prompt: If Terry comes, he will play the violin!
If we go to Paris, we can visit the Eiffel Tower.
What will happen if its mother doesn't feed it?
If I finish my homework at 8, I may watch television for some time.
options: c. Good! Try to finish early.
items.answer: c. Good! Try to finish early.

activities.title: 7. Letter of Advice to the Hospitalised Wolf
activities.instruction: Write a caring letter of advice to the wolf from Little Red Riding Hood.

scaffold.opening: I heard that you are in hospital after the bad experience you had in the forest. I hope you get well soon!
scaffold.body: If I were you, I would stop chasing people and learn to be polite. If you are friendly, other forest animals will like you and play music with you.

activities.title: 8. Personal Safety Tips & Roleplay
activities.instruction: Read the safety guidelines about strangers and formulate advice for personal protection.
rules: Stay away from strangers even if they have familiar faces.
Never get into a car or leave the play area without parental permission.
Always inform parents where you are, who you are with, and when you will return.
